bound.regime: T^eps_alg < C < T^eps_2 for any eps_alg, eps_2 in (0,1)

symbols.eps_2: upper exponent epsilon' in (0,1) for the corruption level

conditions: algorithm has pseudo-regret at most c log(T)/Delta on every stochastic two-arm instance

source.label: thm:lower_bound_1
source.quote: Consider a multi-armed bandits algorithm that has the property that for any stochastic input in the two arm setting, it has pseudo-regret bounded by $c \log(T) / \Delta$, where $\Delta = \abs{\mu_1 - \mu_2}$. For any $\epsilon, \epsilon' \in (0,1)$, there is a corruption level $C$ with $T^\epsilon < C < T^{\epsilon'}$ and a $C$-corrupted instance such that with constant probability the regret is $\Omega(C)$.

results.notes: Regret Omega(C) with constant probability; recorded as realized_regret. Construction uses Bernoulli arms and constant Delta <= 1/6.

bound.regime: T^eps_alg < C < T^eps_2; for all gam > 0

symbols.gam: arbitrary positive constant (paper's delta, not a failure probability)

conditions: algorithm has pseudo-regret at most c log^{1+alpha}(T)/Delta on every stochastic two-arm instance, alpha < 1

source.label: thm:lower_bound_2
source.quote: If a multi-armed bandits algorithm that has the property that for any stochastic input in the two arm setting, it has pseudo-regret bounded by $c \log^{1+\alpha}(T) / \Delta$ for $\alpha < 1$. For any $\epsilon, \epsilon' \in (0,1)$, there is a corruption level $C$ with $T^\epsilon < C < T^{\epsilon'}$ and a $C$-corrupted instance such that $\E[\regret^+] = \Omega(T^{\epsilon - \delta})$ for all $\delta > 0$.

results.notes: Quantity is expected positive part of the realized regret, E[max(Reg,0)].
